title: Homework
description: YAML front matter of course/assessments/homework/HW0N.md. A homework that spans one or more units (Q-026). A manifest of item id references plus its own metadata; items live under course/assessments/items/.

id.description: e.g. 'HW01'. Not per-unit — homework spans units.

units.description: Units this homework assesses. Every referenced item's `unit` must be one of these (rule `homework_units_declared`).

items.description: Ordered list of item ids. Items are referenced, not copied — each must carry `homework` in its `usage` array (rule `homework_item_usage`).

total_minutes.description: Declared time budget. `homework_budget_fits` warns if the sum of items' `est_minutes` drifts outside tolerance.

allowed_tools.description: Open strings. Every tool name must be declared in `course.yaml`'s `tools:` map (HW-D03) — `homework_tools_declared` warns if not. Same shape as in-class `allowed_activity_types`: extensible per-course without forking the framework.

answer_release.description: `graded_answer_release_safe` errors when `purpose: graded` combines with `with_homework` (Q-002 sideways).

status.description: Lifecycle status of this file. `draft` — work-in-progress, written by the pipeline before Gate 2 approval. `shipped` — the file has been approved and is part of the course. Absent means shipped (default; the field only needs to be set to explicitly mark draft state). Convention introduced by HW-Q03 and set by /create-homework's Gate 2 flow. TARGET / FUTURE BEHAVIOR: draft-aware validation (drafts excluded from shipped-homework completeness checks like `assessment_scheme_complete`) is not yet implemented in the Python validator. Today the field is documentary — it marks intent for teachers, git history, and other tooling — and the validator treats draft and shipped files identically. See HW-D01 addendum and HW-Q03 for the target behavior.
